objective: Expose a reusable JSON-fetch hook whose latest active effect alone owns data,error and loading.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: React effect cleanup and stale request guards remain supported practice.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Implements reusable loading,error,recovery and JSON results.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Transfers ownership of asynchronous work across URL changes and unmounts.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Level21 builds on prior request displays with a genuinely reusable hook.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Prevents stale responses and failures from replacing current results.

defects: Original hook is not exported and only the constant App URL is tested;an effect that ignores URL changes falsely passes.
Reference/senior rely solely on abort and junior has no invalidation;no active guard prevents controlled late body work from publishing an obsolete result.
rationale: Make the named public hook contract explicit and preserve combined-state,three-state and reducer approaches. Each effect invalidates its own active flag in cleanup before optional abort;guard success,error and loading completion. Junior also clears old data on a new request. Current failures,including an active AbortError,finish loading with a message;obsolete failures are ignored. A controlled transport separates headers from JSON completion and deliberately ignores abort so A→B→A ownership is observable without claiming native fetch JSON ignores abort. Verify literal arbitrary JSON identity,null/false,HTTP/JSON/network errors,recovery,independent calls and remounts. Existing App success/nonOK/null/network cases remain. No cache,retry,SSR or response-shape API was added.

objective: Persist JSON state after commits while preserving updater semantics,falsy data and usable state through storage errors.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Lazy state reads,pure updates and effect persistence are current React foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Builds a useful persistent setting/counter with blocked/full storage handling.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Transfers missing-versus-falsy,serialization and state updater purity.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Level21 fits browser persistence after state/effect fundamentals.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Prevents lost values,wrong keys,crashes and render-time external writes.

defects: Reference/junior do not guard invalid JSON or storage failures;the junior serializes the setter argument rather than the resolved functional update.
Senior writes localStorage inside a React state updater,which must remain pure and may run during rendering.
Original count-only nonfalsy cases accept hardcoded keys and treating valid falsy data as missing.
rationale: Make the hook a named export and scope it to fixed-per-mount keys and finite JSON data;no cross-tab or dynamic-key rehydration was invented. Keep distinct simple,expanded and read-helper/stable-wrapper answers. Read lazily with fallback only on missing/read/parse errors;write in guarded commit effects;normal state setters accept queued functions. Probe two queued updater operations,retained setter,object/array values,zero/false/empty/null,invalid JSON,getItem/setItem failures,two keys,parent renders,unrelated storage and remounts. A portable method descriptor spy confirms calls and detects writes while a hook render processes queued state. Complete hint example and comment holes remain usable. Native Chromium additionally caught comment-only catch blocks stripped to invalid syntax on the shipped junior/senior boards,despite tolerant server transpilation. Replace those comment-only bodies with empty catch blocks and recheck the actual served strings in both runners. Initial native failure and focused import/function diagnostics remain historical evidence.
